title: mcp: list_actions lists one action once per object it is bound to (invite_user ×4), and run_action by its listed name is refused as ambiguous
body:
Filing category: ① product defect.
reach: public entry `/api/v1/mcp` `tools/call list_actions` / `run_action`, measured once on `objectos-ee` (cloud `ff373e02`, framework `d7c3d44e`) and on a maintainer-provided environment.
Batch-of: 15 cards filed together from one MCP capability test session (2026-11-11; 6 in cloud, 9 in objectstack).

## Business reason

An agent asked to "invite zhangsan@example.com" picks `invite_user` from `list_actions` and calls it; the call is refused and it must guess which of four identical entries to name. Every platform action bound to several system objects behaves this way.

## What happens

`list_actions` returns `invite_user` four times — on `sys_user`, `sys_organization`, `sys_member`, `sys_invitation` — with near-identical descriptions (also `add_team_member` twice). `run_action({ actionName: 'invite_user', params: { email, role } })` → `VALIDATION_ERROR: Action 'invite_user' exists on multiple objects (sys_user, sys_organization, sys_member, sys_invitation); pass objectName to disambiguate`. With `objectName: 'sys_user'` it runs.

## Expected

Either one entry per invokable operation, or `run_action` resolves an action whose bindings are the same operation without asking; at minimum `list_actions` marks which entry to call.

Reader who acts: the seat that owns `packages/mcp` action tools (or the runtime action registry, if the duplication starts there).
Dedupe: `repo:objectstack-ai/objectstack is:issue list_actions duplicate invite_user ambiguous` → 0.
